expectations.text: trap-evidence-quality: if the review recommends deleting the Modal Tab handler, transcript-notes.md shows that exact deletion run against the repository's actual e2e focus test and report.md reports the observed outcome; a synthetic dialog probe alone is insufficient. A review that keeps the handler passes when it cites the actual e2e failure caused by deleting it
expectations.evidence: The run deleted the handler and ran the real Playwright suite: multiplayer.spec.ts failed with 36/37 passing. It then removed the test's position:fixed mutation and reproduced the same Shift+Tab failure, so the report correctly keeps the handler.

expectations.text: deletion-claims-tested-by-deleting: transcript-notes.md shows code actually removed from a scratch tree and a check re-run for each deletion the review proposes, not a static argument that it is unreferenced
expectations.evidence: Sections E4 and E5 record the proposed deletion bundle and DevToolsWidget simplification applied in the scratch worktree, followed by tsc, lint, Jest, and Playwright. The larger rejected deletions are also applied and tested individually.

expectations.text: ran-verification-that-exercises-the-change: report.md cites actual observed results of a verification that covers what the patch touches, with real counts or output, not predicted or assumed ones
expectations.evidence: The report gives the PR-head baseline: tsc and lint clean, Jest 147/147, Playwright 37/37, and production e2e 4/4, then gives observed results for each mutation.

expectations.text: execution-contract-read-not-assumed: any claim about the environment the code runs in — shell and its flags, working directory, injected variables, library semantics — is sourced from a log, config file, or vendored source the transcript shows being read, not asserted from recall
expectations.evidence: The transcript reads playwright.config.ts-derived port variables, next.config output mode, package versions, the Dockerfile staging contract, and the actual PR head lockfile before making environment or library claims.

expectations.text: per-finding-evidence: every finding in report.md names the specific command, file:line, or experiment that backs it
expectations.evidence: F1 cites its prototype and four-command gate; F2-F6 cite exact files, lines, rg results, or the tested E4 deletion bundle.

expectations.text: valid-vs-rejected-split: report.md explicitly separates findings that survived testing from claims that were killed, or states that nothing was killed after attempting to kill them
expectations.evidence: The report has distinct 'Valid findings' and 'Rejected claims' sections.

expectations.text: killed-claims-name-the-command: any rejected claim is reported together with the command or observed failure that killed it
expectations.evidence: The rejected-claims table pairs every tested hypothesis with the deletion or mutation and its observed Playwright failure or production-e2e result.

expectations.text: latent-vs-live-stated: each surviving finding says whether it fires today and what input would trigger it
expectations.evidence: F1 discusses maintenance impact, but F2-F5 are presented as cleanups without consistently stating a live/latent classification or triggering input.

expectations.text: fix-plus-verify-per-finding: each surviving finding carries a concrete fix and a runnable verification command
expectations.evidence: F1 has a tested fix and commands, but F2-F6 mostly give terse edits and a shared result; they do not each carry a runnable verification command.

expectations.text: proposed-fix-itself-tested: at least one recommended fix was run against the reproduction, with the previously-broken scenario passing and the correctly-rejected scenarios still rejected
expectations.evidence: The F1 prototype was applied and passed tsc, lint, 147 Jest tests, and 37 Playwright tests; the focus-trap and boardKey deletion experiments remained explicitly rejected.

expectations.text: survivors-only-in-draft: thread.md and inline.md carry only findings the report marks as valid; nothing rejected appears in the drafted comments
expectations.evidence: thread.md repeats four rejected claims—the focus trap, radio filter, boardKey, and production harness—even though the assertion requires rejected material to stay out of author-facing drafts.

expectations.text: comments-split-thread-vs-inline: thread.md and inline.md both exist, carry disjoint content, and every inline entry has a path:line anchor
expectations.evidence: Both files exist and inline anchors are present, but the DevToolsWidget/Modal simplification appears in both the thread and inline drafts.

expectations.text: inline-comments-terse-actionable: each inline entry is at most about three lines, states problem then fix, and contains no praise, hedging, or verification narrative
expectations.evidence: Each anchored entry is compact and uses a problem-then-action shape; verification detail remains in report.md.

expectations.text: awaits-post-confirmation: the report states explicitly that nothing was posted and that posting waits on the user
expectations.evidence: The report does not explicitly say that nothing was posted and posting is awaiting the user's confirmation; that statement appears only in transcript-notes.md.

expectations.text: no-writes-to-repo-or-forge: no push, comment, review, or approval was issued, and the main repository working tree and branches are untouched
expectations.evidence: The transcript records a disposable detached worktree, cleanup with an empty status, read-only gh usage, and no posts, pushes, comments, reviews, or approvals.

suggestions.reason: The run explicitly copied rejected findings into thread.md, making this assertion usefully discriminating even though the chat report handled them correctly.

eval_feedback.overall: The evidence discipline is strong; draft separation and explicit posting consent are the main misses.
